Published November 25, 2026

If you're looking for someone to build your Squarespace website, it's hard to tell who's good from a Google search. Most "best Squarespace designers" lists I've seen focus on the UK, so this one is for small businesses in the US.

Full disclosure

I'm a Squarespace designer myself, and I've included my own studio on this list. I also worked at NAV Creative for 5 years before I started my own studio. Everyone else was picked using the criteria below.

How I picked

  • Based in the US. Easier time zones, and they know how US small businesses work.

  • Real client reviews. Every designer here has a rating of 4.9 or higher from verified clients on the Squarespace Marketplace.

  • Squarespace is their main platform. They build on Squarespace every day.

  • Active on the Squarespace Marketplace. As of November 2026.

The list isn't ranked. The right designer depends on your business, your budget and what you need, so I've noted what each one is best for. Reviews and starting prices are from each designer's Squarespace Marketplace profile.

Location: Monterey, California
Best for: small businesses that want a clean site with SEO set up from the start
Starting price: $1,500 (Website in a Day), custom sites from $3,000

That's me. I'm a Squarespace Circle Platinum Partner and I've built more than 350 websites. I work with therapists, nonprofits, law firms, photographers and other small businesses, and I also do SEO, Google Ads and monthly website maintenance. You can see some of my work in my portfolio.

Location: St. Louis, Missouri

Starting price: $1,000

Byler Media is a Squarespace Circle Platinum Partner that specializes in WordPress to Squarespace conversions. They've worked with more than 250 clients, from local businesses to online stores, and also offer video production and photography.

Starting price: $1,500
Reviews: 4.98 from 198 reviews on the Squarespace Marketplace

Location: Detroit, Michigan
Best for: artists, restaurants and creative small businesses
Starting price: $2,500
Reviews: 4.99 from 99 reviews on the Squarespace Marketplace

Nicole Cobb is a Squarespace Circle Platinum designer who has built custom Squarespace sites since 2016, with more than 200 projects. Every site comes with a written guide and a recorded video walkthrough, and she offers branding and logo design too.

Location: Omaha, Nebraska

How to choose between them

  • Look at sites like yours. Ask to see a few sites they've built for businesses similar to yours.

  • Get the price in writing. Number of pages, rounds of changes and the total, before you start.

  • Ask about SEO. Find out what's included so your site can show up on Google from day one.

  • Ask about training. You should be able to update your own site once it's done.

  • Check their Squarespace Circle status. Circle partners can get you a discount on your Squarespace plan.

If you're still working out your budget, my post on how much a Squarespace website costs in 2026 breaks down the plans, add-ons and design costs.

FAQ

How much does a Squarespace designer cost?

Most of the designers on this list start between $1,000 and $3,500 for a new site. Bigger custom sites and agencies cost more. My Squarespace cost post has the full breakdown.

What is a Squarespace Circle Platinum Partner?

Squarespace Circle is Squarespace's program for professional designers. Platinum is the highest level, based on how many paying Squarespace sites a designer manages. Platinum partners can get clients 25% off a new yearly Squarespace plan.

Should I hire a freelancer or an agency?

A freelancer usually costs less and you work with the same person the whole time. An agency has a bigger team and can take on more, like marketing, video or ongoing support. Both kinds are on this list.

title: I Built a Squarespace Plugin: Meet OptionKit (Product Options With Prices)
excerpt: For years, when a client asked “can customers add engraving for $15?”, I had to say no. So my studio built the plugin I kept wishing existed. Here’s what it does and how it works.
seoTitle: OptionKit: Squarespace Product Options With Prices
seoDescription: After years of telling clients "Squarespace can't do that," my studio built OptionKit: engraving, gift wrap, custom text and photo uploads, with prices.
body:
I have a confession.

For years, there was one question from clients that I dreaded:

"Can customers add engraving for $15?"

Or gift wrap for $5. Or a name on a cake. Or a photo on a mug.

And every time, I had to say some version of: "Squarespace can't really do that. We can fake it with variants... or you could move to Shopify."

I hated that answer. I move people TO Squarespace so they can run their own website without calling a developer. Telling them to leave over one missing feature felt wrong.

The last straw was a client with a small shop who wanted customers to type a name for engraving and pay a little extra for it. I spent an afternoon trying every workaround I knew. At the end of it I thought: why doesn't this just exist?

So my studio built the thing I kept wishing existed. It's called OptionKit, and it's out now.

What Is OptionKit?

OptionKit is a plugin that adds product options with prices to Squarespace stores.

Your customer picks what they want on the product page. The price updates as they go. And then they pay for all of it in your normal Squarespace cart and checkout.

It lives under a new sister brand to Clementine called JuiceKit. (Yes, we stuck with the fruit theme. 🍊)

What Can You Add to a Product?

There are seven kinds of options, and you can mix them on one product:

  • Text field: "Name to engrave." Free, a set price, or priced per letter.

  • Text box: A longer gift message or special instructions.

  • Checkbox: "Add laser engraving, +$15."

  • Dropdown, buttons, or color swatches: "Frame: Oak, Walnut, Black." Each choice can have its own price.

  • Quantity: "Extra candles, $0.75 each."

  • File upload: A photo, a logo, or a design file sent with the order.

  • Info text: A note between options, like "Made to order: ships in 2 weeks."

And a few things that make it feel polished:

  • Options can show only when they apply. The font choice only appears after "Add engraving" is checked.

  • You can set limits, so nobody orders a 90-letter engraving.

  • It matches your site. Options use your template's fonts and colors, on phones and computers.

How Does It Charge for Options?

This is the clever part, so stick with me.

Squarespace can only charge for products. So each option with a price becomes a small product in your store, like "Laser engraving, $15," on a page that isn't in your menu. OptionKit creates those for you.

When a customer adds a cutting board with engraving, OptionKit adds the engraving to the cart in the same click.

Squarespace does the rest - the cart, discount codes, taxes, checkout, the order, the email. Nothing about your checkout changes.

On the order, you see exactly what each customer chose, right next to the item it belongs to. So two boards with two different names stay two clear jobs.

Who Is It For?

Anyone on Squarespace 7.1 who sells something customers personalize:

  • Engravers and woodworkers (see the engraving setup)

  • Bakeries (custom cakes)

  • Florists (flowers)

  • Framers and print shops (framing)

  • Embroiderers (monograms)

How Long Does Setup Take?

About half an hour. There's no code to write.

  1. Build your options. Start from a template like Engraving or Custom cake, with a preview right next to it.

  2. Connect your store. Paste one line into Squarespace's Code Injection, once.

  3. Publish. Your options are on your store in about a minute.

After that, every change is one click. Nothing to paste again.

What Does It Cost?

  • Free on your site's squarespace.com address, for as long as you like. Build and test everything.

  • Free for 14 days on your own domain, with no card.

  • Then $12 a month or $120 a year per store.

There are no per-order fees and no limits on products or options. One $15 engraving pays for the month.

What It Doesn't Do (Yet)

I'd rather be upfront:

  • It's for Squarespace 7.1. It doesn't work on 7.0.

  • You need a plan with Code Injection. That's Core, Plus, or Advanced, or an older Business or Commerce plan.

  • No live preview on the product photo yet. Customers see their choices and the price update, but they don't see their text on the photo. That's coming soon.

Try It

The fastest way to understand it is to play with it. Try the live demo store here - check a box, type a name, upload a photo, and watch the price change.

Then try OptionKit free on your own store.

Final Thoughts

I built this because I needed it for my own clients. Now, when someone asks "can customers add engraving for $15?", I finally get to say yes.

If you'd like OptionKit set up for you, or you want a whole store designed around it, book a free consultation. I'd love to see what you're selling.
summary: For years, when a client asked “can customers add engraving for $15?”, I had to say no. So my studio built the plugin I kept wishing existed. Here’s what it does and how it works.

Frequently Asked Questions About AI Headshots

Are AI headshots good enough for LinkedIn?

Yes, if you use a good generator. A cheap one can leave you looking like a heavily filtered video game character, which isn't what you want for networking. My best results from PhotoPacks.AI looked like real photos of me, and I'd use them on LinkedIn, my website's About page or my email signature.

Do recruiters care if your headshot is AI-generated?

From what I've seen, most people care more about whether your photo looks professional and actually looks like you than how it was made. An AI photo can hurt you if you show up to an interview looking very different from your picture, or if the photo has obvious AI mistakes like blurry eyes or strange lighting. Pick one that looks natural and looks like you.

How much do AI headshot generators cost?

Most paid AI headshot generators cost somewhere between $15 and $40, and you usually get anywhere from 40 to 100+ photos with different outfits, poses and backgrounds. A local photographer usually charges $200 to $500 or more for a basic studio session, so AI is a much cheaper option.

Is there a good free AI headshot generator?

There are more free options now, including tools from Canva and Adobe, and Profile Pic Maker has a free tier. I haven't tested the free ones with my own photos yet, so I can't tell you how they compare. If you just need a quick placeholder, they could be worth a try. For a LinkedIn photo that really looks like you, PhotoPacks.AI is what I'd use.

Do AI headshots look fake?

They definitely can. As you saw above, the cheaper generators gave me the wrong eye color, waxy skin and outlines around my face. The better tools have gotten a lot more realistic, and my best PhotoPacks.AI photos looked like real photos of me.

How many photos do I need to upload for AI headshots?

It depends on the tool. PhotoPacks.AI asks for 10, and ProfilePicture.AI wanted at least 20 when I tested it. A good mix helps: close-ups, chest-up shots, different angles and different lighting. Skip group photos, heavy filters, and photos where sunglasses or a hat cover your face.

Which AI generator is best for people with glasses?

AI often has trouble with glasses. It can warp the frames or add glare that hides your eyes. In my test, PhotoPacks.AI handled glasses the best. The frames kept their shape and my eyes looked normal behind the lenses.

Tip: include several photos of yourself wearing your glasses from different angles, so the AI can see how they sit on your face.

Can I use AI headshots on my Squarespace website?

Yes, but check the size. Squarespace recommends images between 1500 and 2500 pixels wide, and small 512px files will look blurry on a computer screen. PhotoPacks.AI gives you high-resolution images, which work well on a website. If you want a wide banner, you can use Canva or Photoshop to extend the background, or pick a headshot with a plain background that's easy to crop.

Is your website holding you hostage?

It’s a specific kind of panic. You need to update your pricing or change a team member's photo, but you stare at your dashboard and freeze. You're scared that if you click the wrong button, the whole site breaks.

So, you email your developer. You wait three days. You pay an expensive hourly invoice. And you repeat the cycle next month.

If this sounds like you, you aren't alone.

As a Squarespace Expert, about 50% of my clients come to me with an existing WordPress website that they hate. They aren't looking for a new design just for fun; they are looking for freedom.

They tell me, “Mali, it’s too complicated. I’m scared to touch it.”

My design philosophy is simple: No one should be held hostage by their website platform.

Here is why migrating from WordPress to Squarespace is the best business move you can make in 2026, and why I refuse to build sites that require a developer to maintain.

1. The Hidden Cost of WordPress Maintenance

When you hired your original designer, they probably told you WordPress was the "professional" choice. They didn't mention the upkeep.

To keep a WordPress site secure, you (or a hired pro) need to:

  • Update plugins weekly (and fix them when they break your layout).

  • Run security backups so you don't get hacked.

  • Pay for managed hosting fees.

I’ve had clients paying a high hourly rate to developers just for basic "maintenance" tasks. That’s money that should be going into your marketing, not keeping the lights on.

When we migrate your site to Squarespace, that maintenance budget drops to $0.

Squarespace handles all the security, updates, and hosting in the background. You never have to pay me to "update a plugin" again.

2. "Can I Edit My Own Website?" (Yes, Finally)

This is the main reason I move therapists, law firms, and small business owners to Squarespace.

On WordPress, the dashboard looks like the cockpit of an alien spaceship. On Squarespace, the dashboard looks like... a drag-and-drop canvas.

  • I provide a recorded 1-on-1 training session.

3. But Will I Lose My Google Ranking? (SEO Migration)

This is the big fear. “If I move, will I disappear from Google?”

Not if you hire a Squarespace SEO Expert.

When I migrate a client from WordPress to Squarespace, I don't just copy-paste the text. I perform a full SEO Migration:

  1. URL Mapping: I make sure your old links (like /about-us) redirect to your new links.

  2. Metadata Transfer: I move all your hard-earned SEO titles and descriptions.

  3. Content Cleanup: We fix broken images and messy code that was slowing down your old WordPress site.

In many cases, my clients see their rankings go UP after switching because the new site is faster, mobile-friendly, and easier for Google to read.

Final Thoughts: Take Back Control

You shouldn't have to wait a week to post a new service. You shouldn't have to pay a "ransom" in hourly fees just to keep your website online.

If you are ready to migrate your WordPress site to Squarespace and finally feel confident in your online presence, I can help.

title: The Hidden Costs of Squarespace: A 2026 Pricing Breakdown (Transaction Fees, Email & Scheduling)

seoTitle: Squarespace Pricing Guide 2026: Hidden Fees, Transaction Costs & Add-Ons
seoDescription: Confused by Squarespace fees? I break down the real cost of Squarespace Payments, transaction fees, Acuity Scheduling, and Member Areas in this 2026 guide.
body:
Note: All prices listed below are for the US and were last checked on November 25, 2026, after Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026. Pricing changes often, so I’ve included links to the official pages so you can always check the live rates.

Let’s be real: Trying to figure out the actual price of a Squarespace website can feel like a scavenger hunt.

You look at the main pricing page and see a base monthly fee. You think, "Okay, $29/month. That fits my budget."

But that base price is just the starting line.

Once you actually start building your business, the costs begin to layer on. You realize that selling a product triggers a transaction fee. Sending a branded newsletter is an extra subscription. Want to let clients book appointments? That’s another add-on cost.

Suddenly, your $29/month bill looks a lot different.

The problem is that Squarespace lists all these fees on five different support pages, making it nearly impossible to get a clear picture of your total overhead.

I wanted to stop the madness. So, I decided to consolidate it all right here. I’ve pulled the data from the commerce page, the scheduling page, and the email marketing page to bring it all into one easy-to-read guide.

My goal is to make this as simple as possible so you don’t have to have 15 tabs open just to figure out what your website will actually cost.

Here is exactly what you are paying for when you build a Squarespace site in 2026: from the base "rent" to the necessary "utilities" all in one place.

1. The "Rent": Monthly Hosting Fees

First, you have the base cost. This is just to have your website exist on the internet. Currently, Squarespace has 4 main plans: Basic, Core, Plus, and Advanced. Paid yearly, they cost $19, $29, $49 and $99 a month. If you want the full picture, including what it costs to have a site designed, see my post on how much a Squarespace website costs.

  • The Basic Plan is great for portfolios and simple brochures.

  • The Core/Plus/Advanced Plans unlock more features like e-commerce analytics and better merchandising tools.

But the monthly fee is just the start. If you plan to sell anything (services, products, or donations), you need to know about the fees below.

2. The "Hidden" Fees: Getting Paid

This is the part that usually trips people up. There are actually two types of fees that come out of your sales.

A. Credit Card Processing Fees (The Bank's Cut)

No matter what plan you are on, if a client pays you with a credit card, the processor takes a cut. You cannot avoid this (it’s how Visa/Mastercard make money).

You generally have three options for processing payments:

Option 1: Squarespace Payments (The New Standard)

Squarespace recently launched their own processor to compete with Stripe. The fee depends on which hosting plan you are on:

  • Basic Plan: 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

  • Core Plan: 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

  • Plus Plan: 2.7% + $0.30 per transaction

  • Advanced Plan: 2.5% + $0.30 per transaction (Best for high volume!)

> Check the most updated Squarespace Transaction Fees here.

Option 2: Stripe

If you stick with the classic Stripe integration, the standard US rate is usually 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction, regardless of your Squarespace plan.
> Check current Stripe Pricing here.

Option 3: PayPal

If you allow clients to pay via PayPal, their fees are slightly different, typically 2.99% + a fixed fee (which varies by country).
> Check current PayPal Business Fees here.

B. The Squarespace "Transaction Fee" (The Platform Cut)

Heads up: This is separate from the credit card fee!

  • If you are on the BASIC Plan: Squarespace takes an additional 2% cut of every sale.

    • My professional advice: The Basic plan is okay for "proof of concept" if you are on a tight budget. But once you start making regular sales, that 2% adds up fast. It’s usually better to upgrade to the Core plan (where this fee drops to 0%) to save money in the long run.

  • If you are on Core, Plus, or Advanced: Squarespace takes 0%. You only pay the credit card processing fee.

3. The Add-Ons: Courses, Scheduling & Email

These features are powerful, but they are not included in your base hosting bill.

Selling Courses (Member Areas)

Want to create a paywall or sell a digital course? Squarespace calls these "Member Areas." Just like the commerce fees, they take a percentage of your course sales depending on your plan:

  • Basic Plan: 7% fee

  • Core Plan: 5% fee

  • Plus Plan: 1% fee

  • Advanced Plan: 0% fee

Again, if you plan to sell a $500 course, do NOT stay on the Basic plan, or you'll be donating 7% of that straight to Squarespace!

Booking Appointments (Acuity Scheduling)

If you are a therapist, coach, or yoga studio, you probably know Acuity Scheduling. Squarespace acquired them a while back. It integrates perfectly, but it requires a separate subscription.

  • Starter Plan (~$16/mo annually): Great for solo business owners.

  • Standard Plan (~$27/mo annually): Adds text message reminders (crucial for reducing no-shows!) and subscriptions/packages.

  • Premium Plan (~$55/mo annually): Needed for HIPAA compliance, multiple time zones, and multiple staff calendars.

> Check the most updated Acuity Pricing here.

Email Campaigns (Newsletters)

You can collect email addresses for free using a Newsletter Block on your site. But if you want to send pretty, branded emails directly from Squarespace, you need an Email Campaigns subscription.

  • The Free Trial: You can send up to 3 blast emails (5,000 sends per email) to test it out. Note: You don't get automated emails on the trial.

  • Paid Plans: Start at roughly $8/mo (annually) for 500 emails/month.

  • Why pay? It allows you to set up automations. For example, if someone downloads your "Free Guide," Squarespace can automatically email it to them. The price scales up based on how many emails you send (up to $118/mo for 500k emails).

> Check the rates at the bottom of the Squarespace Email Pricing page.

Final Thoughts: Don't Let the Math Scare You

I know… it looks like a lot of numbers. But here is the good news: You can start small.

Most of my clients start on the Core Plan (to avoid the 2% transaction fee) and add Acuity or Email Campaigns later as they grow.

The beauty of Squarespace is that everything is in one place. You don't need a separate Mailchimp account, a separate WordPress hosting bill, and a separate Calendly invoice. It’s all under one roof.

Confused about which plan is right for you? You don't have to figure it out alone. Book a free consultation and I’ll help you pick the setup that saves you the most money based on your business goals.
summary: Does Squarespace take a cut of your sales? How much is Acuity really? As a Squarespace expert, I see clients get confused by these fees constantly. I’m breaking down the real cost of running a site in 2026 so you can budget with confidence.

title: How Much Does a Squarespace Website Cost in 2026? Plans, Fees and Design Costs
excerpt: Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026. Here's what a Squarespace website costs now, from the plan and add-ons to hiring a designer, with my own prices.
seoTitle: How Much Does a Squarespace Website Cost? (2026 Prices)
seoDescription: Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026. Plans now cost $19 to $99 a month. Here's what a site really costs in year one, on your own or with a designer.
imageAlt: A Squarespace website I designed for a mediation practice, shown on a laptop
body:
Published February 18, 2026 · Updated November 25, 2026 with Squarespace's new prices

Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026, so a lot of the numbers you'll find online are out of date. I build Squarespace websites for a living, so I went through Squarespace's own pricing pages and added up what a website actually costs now, from the plan itself to the extras people don't expect. I also included what it costs to have someone design it for you, with my own prices.

The short answer

A Squarespace plan costs $19 to $99 a month if you pay for the year up front, or $25 to $139 if you pay month to month. Most small businesses I work with use the Core plan, which is $29 a month, or $348 a year.

If you hire a designer, add a one-time design cost on top of that. My Website-in-a-Day is $1,500 and my custom websites start at $3,000. Big agencies usually charge $10,000 or more.

All prices are in US dollars and come from squarespace.com and acuityscheduling.com, checked on November 25, 2026. Prices before tax.

Squarespace plans and prices in 2026

Every plan includes hosting, a free SSL certificate, mobile-friendly templates and 24/7 support. Every plan also lets you sell. The differences are mostly in the fees you pay when you sell and in the extra store and marketing tools.

PlanPaid yearlyPaid monthlyCost per yearOnline store feeCard rate
Basic$19/mo$25/mo$2282%2.9% + 30¢
Core$29/mo$39/mo$3480%2.9% + 30¢
Plus$49/mo$65/mo$5880%2.7% + 30¢
Advanced$99/mo$139/mo$1,1880%2.5% + 30¢

"Cost per year" is the yearly price. If you pay monthly instead, Basic works out to $300 a year and Core to $468. Card rates are for Squarespace Payments with standard cards. American Express and some business cards are 3.2% + 30¢ on every plan. You can see the full list on Squarespace's pricing page.

What changed in July 2026

Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026 by up to 26%, depending on the plan. On yearly billing, Basic went from $16 to $19 a month and Core went from $23 to $29 a month (PetaPixel covered it here). If you signed up before then, you'll see the new price when your plan renews.

Which plan do you need?

  • Basic ($19/mo): Fine for a portfolio or a simple site where you aren't selling much. It only allows 2 contributors, and Squarespace takes an extra 2% of anything you sell through your online store.

  • Core ($29/mo): This is the one I recommend to most of my clients. There's no 2% store fee, you get unlimited contributors, and it comes with a free year of business email through Google Workspace.

  • Plus ($49/mo): Worth it if you run a growing online store. Card fees drop to 2.7% + 30¢, and the fee on courses and memberships drops from 5% to 1%.

  • Advanced ($99/mo): For high-volume shops and course creators. It has the lowest card rate and no fee at all on courses and memberships.

A quick way to decide between Basic and Core: Core costs $120 more a year than Basic. The 2% store fee on Basic costs you $120 once you sell about $6,000 a year through your website. If you expect to sell more than that, Core is the cheaper plan.

Other costs to budget for

The plan price isn't the whole bill. Here's what else usually comes up.

Your domain name

If you pay for a plan yearly, Squarespace gives you a free domain for the first year. After that it renews at the regular price, which is $22 a year for a .com on Squarespace Domains. If you already own a domain somewhere else, you can connect it to your site instead.

Business email

Core, Plus and Advanced include a free year of Google Workspace, so you can have an email like you@yourbusiness.com. After the first year, Google Workspace is billed per person, per month.

Card processing fees

Whenever someone pays you by card, the payment processor takes a cut. With Squarespace Payments it's 2.9% + 30¢ on Basic and Core, and less on the higher plans. Stripe and PayPal charge their own rates. I break all of these down, including the 2% Basic store fee, in my post on the hidden costs of Squarespace.

Online booking (Acuity Scheduling)

If clients book appointments with you, you'll probably want Acuity Scheduling, which Squarespace owns. It's a separate subscription:

Acuity planPaid yearlyPaid monthlyGood for
Starter$16/mo$20/moOne person with one calendar
Standard$27/mo$34/moText reminders, packages and up to 6 calendars
Premium$55/mo$69/moHIPAA (for therapists and health practices) and up to 36 calendars

If you're a therapist or work in healthcare and need a signed HIPAA agreement, that's only on Premium. Prices are on Acuity's pricing page.

Email newsletters

Collecting email signups on your site is free. Sending newsletters from Squarespace takes an Email Campaigns plan, which starts at $8 a month (paid yearly) for up to 500 emails a month and goes up to $118 a month for 500,000. You can also connect Mailchimp on the Core plan and up.

Courses and memberships

If you sell courses or memberships through Squarespace, there's a fee on each sale: 7% on Basic, 5% on Core, 1% on Plus and 0% on Advanced.

Templates

Squarespace templates are free on every plan. You only pay extra if you buy a third-party template or plugin, which most sites don't need.

What a Squarespace website costs for the first year

Here are three common setups, using yearly billing. These are just the Squarespace costs. Design costs are in the next section.

SetupWhat's includedFirst year
Simple websiteBasic plan, free domain for the first year$228
Service businessCore plan + Acuity Starter$540
Therapy practiceCore plan + Acuity Premium (HIPAA)$1,008

Add card fees if you take payments online. From the second year on, add $22 a year for a .com domain.

What it costs to have a Squarespace website designed

This is the part most people are really asking about. There are three main ways to get your site built, and the costs are very different.

1. Doing it yourself

Design cost: $0, plus your time.

Squarespace makes it look easy, and if you have a good eye for design, you can make a template work. But a lot of my clients come to me after spending weeks on their own site. Things don't line up the way they want, the phone version looks off, and they've spent whole weekends searching for how to fix it.

A DIY site usually takes 40 to 80 hours. If your time is worth $100 an hour, that's $4,000 to $8,000 of your time, and it's easy to miss SEO settings you didn't know existed.

2. Hiring a freelance Squarespace designer

Design cost: about $1,500 to $5,000, depending on the size of the site.

This is where I work. You talk to the person building your site directly, and a site usually takes days or weeks instead of months. A good freelancer will also set up your SEO, connect your booking or payment tools and show you how to make edits yourself.

3. Hiring a big agency

Design cost: $10,000 to $25,000 or more.

Agencies give you a whole team, like a copywriter, a designer and a developer, and their work is often beautiful. I've seen quotes my clients got from agencies before they came to me, and they're a lot for a small business. Agency projects also tend to take 3 to 4 months.

How to choose a Squarespace designer

Whoever you hire, here's what I'd check before you sign anything:

  • Sites like yours. Ask to see a few sites they've built for businesses similar to yours.

  • Reviews from real clients. Squarespace's own Marketplace and 99designs both show reviews from people who hired the designer through them.

  • A clear price. Get the number of pages, rounds of changes and the total in writing before you start.

  • SEO setup. Ask what's included, so your site can show up on Google from day one.

  • Training. You should be able to update your own site once it's done.

  • Squarespace Circle status. Circle partners can get you a discount on your Squarespace plan.

As for me, I've built more than 350 websites over the past 7+ years, and I'm a Squarespace Circle Platinum Partner. I have 115 reviews on my Squarespace Marketplace profile (listed as Clementine Studio) and a 5.0 rating from 100+ reviews on 99designs. You can see some of my work in my portfolio.

A few reviews from the Squarespace Marketplace

"Mali was fantastic. I'm very happy with the website and she made the process so easy."

"I had a great experience working with Clementine Studio on my website updates. She listened carefully to what I needed and suggested an approach that worked even better than my original idea."

My prices

I used to not list my prices, which I know is frustrating when you're trying to budget. So here they are.

ServicePriceWhat you get
Website-in-a-Day$1,5001 to 5 pages on Squarespace, built in one day with your logo and colors. Changes until the end of the day and a training call. You'll need your text and photos ready.
Custom WebsiteFrom $3,0005+ pages on Squarespace, Shopify or WordPress, in about 3 to 4 weeks. 3 rounds of revisions, SEO setup and a training call.
Hourly Help$150/hrUpdates, layout changes and troubleshooting on a site you already have.
Monthly MaintenanceAbout $300/moSend me questions or changes anytime, and I'll fix things if something goes wrong.

Your Squarespace plan is separate from my design fee. As a Circle Platinum Partner, I can get you 25% off a new yearly Squarespace plan, which brings Core from $348 down to $261 for the year. You can see everything I offer on my services page.

How to spend less on Squarespace

  • Pay for the year up front. Squarespace says yearly billing saves up to 36%, and it comes with the free domain.

  • Pick your plan based on how much you'll sell. If you'll sell more than about $6,000 a year through your site, Core costs less than Basic.

  • Add things when you need them. You can start on Core and add Acuity or Email Campaigns later, as your business grows.

  • Use the free trial. Every site starts with a 14-day free trial, and you don't need a credit card for it.

Is Squarespace worth the price?

For most small businesses, I think so. Hosting, security and support are included, so you aren't paying separately for hosting and plugins or keeping them updated. Your booking and newsletters can also live in the same place as your website.

It isn't the cheapest option if all you need is one page and you're comfortable building it yourself. But it's the platform I build most of my clients' sites on, because they can update it on their own once it's done.

Frequently asked questions

Is Squarespace free?

No. Squarespace doesn't have a free plan, but every site starts with a 14-day free trial, and you don't need a credit card to start one. You'll need a paid plan to publish your site.

How much is Squarespace per month?

Squarespace costs $19, $29, $49 or $99 a month when you pay for the year up front, or $25, $39, $65 or $139 a month when you pay monthly.

How much does a Squarespace website cost per year?

The plan alone is $228 to $1,188 a year on yearly billing. Most small businesses pay about $348 a year for the Core plan, plus any add-ons like Acuity Scheduling.

Does Squarespace include hosting and a domain?

Hosting is included on every plan. A domain is free for the first year when you pay yearly. After that, a .com renews at $22 a year.

How much does it cost to hire a Squarespace designer?

Freelance Squarespace designers usually charge about $1,500 to $5,000 for a full website, and agencies charge $10,000 or more. My Website-in-a-Day is $1,500, and my custom websites start at $3,000.

How do I find a good Squarespace designer?

Start with Squarespace's own Marketplace, where you can compare designers' portfolios, starting prices and client reviews. Then ask a few of them for examples of sites like yours and a written price before you decide.

Did Squarespace raise its prices?

Yes. In July 2026, Squarespace raised prices by up to 26%. On yearly billing, Basic went from $16 to $19 a month and Core went from $23 to $29.

Can I cancel or change my Squarespace plan?

Yes. You can change or cancel your plan anytime, and the change takes effect at the end of the period you've already paid for.

Want help figuring out your costs?

If you're not sure which plan or add-ons you need, I'm happy to help. Book a free 20-minute consultation and I'll tell you what your website would cost, both on Squarespace and with me.

title: How to Migrate Your Squarespace 5 Website to Squarespace 7.1
excerpt: In this post, I’ll walk you through the general roadmap for migrating from Squarespace 5 to 7.1 - what transfers, what doesn’t, and the most common hang-ups. And if you’d rather not deal with any of it, I offer done-for-you migrations so you can upgrade your site without lifting a finger.
body:
If you're still running your website on Squarespace version 5, you're not alone, but you are on borrowed time.

Squarespace 5 was ahead of its time when it launched. But that was over a decade ago. As of now, Squarespace has stopped offering full support for version 5 sites, and more features are quietly starting to break or disappear.

If your site is your business or portfolio, that’s not a risk worth taking.

To make things trickier, Squarespace 5 and Squarespace 7.1 are completely different platforms under the hood. You can’t just click a button and have everything transfer over - some parts of your site won’t carry over at all, and others need manual cleanup. But I promise, it doesn’t have to be a nightmare.

In this post, I’ll walk you through the general roadmap for migrating from Squarespace 5 to 7.1 - what transfers, what doesn’t, and the most common hang-ups. And if you’d rather not deal with any of it, I offer done-for-you migrations so you can upgrade your site without lifting a finger (or stressing out over URL slugs and broken galleries).

Why Migrate to 7.1?

Squarespace 7.1 isn’t just a facelift - it’s a totally rebuilt platform. You get:

  • Modern, responsive templates

  • Native e-commerce features

  • Integrated email marketing

  • Site-wide style editing (no more one-page-at-a-time frustration)

  • Built-in SEO and analytics tools

Whether you’re running a blog, portfolio, or full-blown business site, 7.1 is easier to use, more powerful, and future-proof.

How the Migration Works (Big Picture)

Here’s a quick rundown of what migrating from Squarespace 5 to 7.1 usually looks like:

  1. Start fresh with a Squarespace 7 trial. This creates a new workspace where your 5.0 content can live.

  2. Import your old content. Blog posts, image galleries, and standard pages usually carry over. (But not everything does - more on that in a sec.)

  3. Upgrade that 7.0 trial to 7.1. This gives you access to the latest templates and editing tools.

  4. Clean things up. You’ll need to replace some images, re-style your layout, and manually re-add a few things (like PDFs or footers).

  5. Check your URLs. Keeping your page links consistent helps with SEO and avoids broken links.

  6. Connect your domain + launch. Once everything looks right, it's time to go live and cancel the old site billing.

Sounds simple enough… until you actually open both editors and realize they speak entirely different languages.

What Carries Over (and What Doesn’t)

You can import:

  • HTML pages

  • Blog posts (and comments!)

  • Image galleries

  • Most page content

You can’t import:

  • Custom sidebars or footers

  • File uploads (like PDFs)

  • Markdown formatting

  • Old styles, fonts, or layout settings

  • Anything coded using legacy widgets

Some of this can be rebuilt with new tools in 7.1 - but it takes a trained eye to make it seamless. And if you have older blog content using Markdown or embedded podcast players, you’ll need to update that manually.

Good News: You Don’t Have to Do It Alone

If you’re looking at this process thinking, “Ugh, I don’t have time for this,” that’s exactly where I come in.

I’ve helped clients migrate their Squarespace 5 sites to 7.1 with minimal downtime, no broken links, and a fresh, modern look that feels like an upgrade - not a setback.

I’ll handle the import, the cleanup, the styling, the domain move - all of it. So you can focus on running your business or blog instead of troubleshooting your image library or figuring out what a URL slug is.

Want a Hand With the Migration?

Whether you want to:

  • Modernize your look

  • Sell products or services

  • Improve your SEO

  • Or just stop worrying about outdated tech…

I can help you migrate with zero stress. Just reach out here, and I’ll walk you through the best plan based on your current setup.

title: How to Build a Membership Community on Squarespace (That People Actually Stick With)
excerpt: This guide breaks down how to build a thriving online community using Squarespace Member Areas - perfect for fitness coaches, course creators, or anyone ready to turn their content into a sustainable income stream. From gated content and video libraries to live calls and forums, here’s how to make it all happen (and actually keep people engaged).
seoDescription: This guide breaks down how to build a thriving online community using Squarespace Member Areas - perfect for fitness coaches, course creators, or anyone ready to turn their content into a sustainable income stream.
body:
There’s a reason so many of us are craving real connection online - especially in spaces where we can learn, grow, or feel supported in some kind of transformation.

Whether you're building a workout program, a virtual classroom, or a coaching container, Squarespace + Member Areas makes it surprisingly simple to create a space where your community can gather, stay accountable, and keep showing up.

I’ve helped brands do this in ways that are super user-friendly and beautifully on-brand - and it all lives right on Squarespace.

If this sounds like something you want to build, don’t wait. Book a consultation with me, and let’s map it out.

Step 1: Create a Paywalled Program, Your Way

Squarespace’s Member Areas feature lets you lock content behind a paywall, so you can offer a subscription-based program without needing third-party platforms or complicated tech.

You can:

  • Set up recurring monthly payments or one-time access

  • Drop content monthly or unlock everything at once

  • Offer videos, PDFs, audio recordings, downloadable templates - whatever makes sense for your niche

I’ve seen this work especially well for:

  • Fitness programs with weekly workouts

  • Online schools or creative courses

  • Group coaching programs

  • Private support communities for clients or alumni

Already using Squarespace? Great - you’re halfway there. Let’s turn what you already have into a recurring revenue stream.

Step 2: Build a Content Hub That Delivers Value

This is the heart of the experience - and where many people overcomplicate things. You don’t need a massive library to start. A focused, well-structured hub will go a long way.

Some examples I’ve helped clients launch include:

  • 4 new strength training videos per month

  • A 6-week curriculum that unlocks weekly

  • Pre-recorded breathwork or meditation sessions

  • Monthly templates or design tools for creative businesses

You can build your hub using Squarespace’s built-in page sections or blog layouts. I usually set it up so content is super easy to navigate - organized by week, phase, or topic. And with the ability to add buttons, downloads, and video blocks, the content delivery feels elevated even though the backend is simple.

Want to give members a better sense of momentum? Use blog posts as a time-based release method ("Week 1," "Week 2," etc.), or create a library structure so people can binge content at their own pace.

Not sure how to organize your content or what format works best? I’ve done this dozens of times - let’s talk.

Step 3: Add a Forum to Keep Your Community Talking

One of the easiest ways to build retention? Make sure your members aren’t just interacting with you, but with each other.

I install a third-party tool called Website Toolbox that allows you to embed a full-featured forum right into your Squarespace site. Members can:

  • Ask questions

  • Post their wins or challenges

  • Upload progress videos or photos

  • Keep the conversation going between content drops

This works especially well in fitness programs, course groups, or coaching communities where accountability and support are key. You can even segment by topic or phase.

Want your site to include a built-in community space? I’ll take care of the integration for you. Reach out here.

Step 4: Offer Live Touchpoints (Without the Burnout)

Adding a human layer doesn’t mean you need to be "on" 24/7. What works best long-term is predictable, light-touch engagement:

  • Monthly group Zoom calls or Q&As

  • A pre-recorded welcome message or tutorial

  • Office hour blocks once a month for deeper support

Squarespace Scheduling can help you manage any live session signups, or you can just drop a recurring Zoom link inside your member portal. Keep it simple.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a Commerce plan to use Member Areas?
You can use Member Areas on any Squarespace plan, but the fees vary accordingly. If you’re on the Personal Plan, they take a whopping 7% (don’t forget the credit card transaction fee too), but if you’re on the Commerce Plus plan, that drops down to 1%.

Can I drip content over time?
Yes! You can schedule posts or pages to publish at future dates, or organize them in a weekly layout.

What payment options can I offer?
Squarespace handles major credit cards and can integrate with Squarespace Payments, Stripe or PayPal, depending on your setup.

Can I mix digital product sales with memberships?
Absolutely. You can sell one-off guides, workshops, or merch alongside your membership without disrupting anything.

Do members get their own login?
Yes - they create an account tied to their purchase.

Who This Works Best For

Not every business needs a membership program - but if you:

  • Already have a community forming around your work

  • Want a recurring revenue stream

What is accessibility in terms of web design?

Accessibility refers to the practice of ensuring that websites, digital tools, and other technologies are usable and navigable by people of all abilities, including those with disabilities. This includes but is not limited to visual, auditory, physical, speech, cognitive, and neurological disabilities. Accessibility aims to remove barriers that might prevent individuals from accessing or interacting with digital content and services.

Why is it important for my website to be accessible?

When I'm crafting websites, I'm careful to design them in a way that complies with WCAG & ADA compliant standards. For example, if a client asks for pale blue text on a white background, I’ll double-check the colors using a contrast checker, as it may not be readable to those with a visual impairment. If they don't pass the test, I'll let the client know. Even after I explain how important accessibility is, some clients are insistent on their design choices. And I get it — sometimes accessible design just doesn’t fit a certain aesthetic. With accessiBe in the picture, these kinds of issues could be a thing of the past!

Making your website accessible isn’t just a moral thing; it's a legal thing too! You don't want to find yourself in hot water because your site isn't ADA compliant, trust me. Lawsuits related to web accessibility are no joke, and they can seriously hurt your business. It's not just about avoiding legal trouble; it's about being inclusive and welcoming to all users.

With their free trial, I was able to test accessiBe out for myself. It was super easy to install - just a simple copy/paste of one line of code. They also provide special instructions for Squarespace users.

With accessiBe, you rest assured that your website is WCAG & ADA compliant without having to deal with the hassle of making manual adjustments. This means that as guidelines evolve or new regulations are introduced, your website remains up-to-date and in compliance, minimizing the risk of legal repercussions and ensuring continued accessibility for all users.

In conclusion, accessiBe offers a comprehensive solution for achieving and maintaining website accessibility compliance — and it only takes a few minutes to install! I’m happy to support a company that aims to make the web accessible to all.

title: Does Squarespace Have An SEO Plugin Similar to Yoast in 2023?
excerpt: Yes it does! Using this plugin, Squarespace users can now run scans on each page of their website to give them more insight into what areas to improve to optimize their chances of being favored by Google.
body:
Yoast is a popular plugin that helps WordPress users improve their websites for Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Squarespace users have been long overdue for a similar plugin in the same vein! In April 2023, Henry Purchase, founder of Rough Water Media, released their long-awaited plugin: SEOSpace.

Using this plugin, Squarespace users can now run scans on each page of their website to give them more insight into what areas to improve to optimize their chances of being favored by Google.

I’ve been following Henry Purchase for a few months before the plugin was released. He’s well-versed in both Squarespace and SEO, and has released multiple YouTube helpful videos on his channel on the topic of optimizing for SEO. I’ve found his videos are super informational, and he seems to be very passionate about helping Squarespace users get the most out of the platform without breaking the bank.

I purchased a “DIY Plan” ($9.99/mo) and tested my own website to see how it works. I downloaded the Chrome plugin, put in my targeted keyword “squarespace experts,” and ran a Premium Scan on my homepage. After the scan was complete, it gave me a score: 49/100.

The plugin caught a few issues that were likely holding my page up from being ranked, such as having multiple H1 tags and missing image alt text. I had forgotten that I created a section on the homepage that was only visible on mobile, which included an H1 tag and an image. Nice catch, SEOSpace!

The plugin also used my keyword “squarespace experts,” and caught any instances where it should be placed on my website in order to improve my chances of ranking for it (a Premium Scan perk).

I fixed the outstanding errors, ran the Premium Scan again, and got up to an 89/100. There was one fix that I had missed - my meta description didn’t have enough characters. Once I fixed it, I was tempted to run the scan again just to feel the satisfaction of seeing a perfect score. But I decided against it, since I wanted to save them, as my plan comes with 10 Premium Scans.

I plan to go through each page on my website with my intended keyword to optimize my entire site. I’m still working on my SEO strategy, though, so I feel like that should come first.

Overall Thoughts

I think the emergence of SEOSpace is an awesome start to helping Squarespace users optimize their site for SEO. Their “Free Plan” includes 10 Basic Scans per month, which looks for baseline refinements such as checking broken links, image sizes, meta tags, and other baseline refinements to get your website up to speed. It’s a good place to start if you just want to test the plugin out.

It’s a great quick way to check every page of a Squarespace website for optimization suggestions, and it’s the first of its kind.

If you upgrade to their “DIY Plan,” you’ll be able to enter a keyword and location to get suggestions on where to place them throughout your page.

Henry and his team at SEOSpace are very responsive and open to suggestions as they continue to make improvements and iron out kinks since their first launch date. With the “DIY Plan,” you get access to the SEOSpace community, where you can offer suggestions, get help, and connect with other SEOSpace users.

I plan to upgrade to the highest tier “Agency Plan” to see how the “Discover search keywords” function works once I have my SEO strategy in place. With this plan, it looks like there’s some additional features that are on their way as well, such as automated monitoring, scans, and reports. I’ll report back when I do.
summary: Yes it does! Using this plugin, Squarespace users can now run scans on each page of their website to give them more insight into what areas to improve to optimize their chances of being favored by Google.

title: Should You Update Squarespace To The Latest Version?
excerpt: Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.
body:
Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.

There’s no doubt that websites built on the new Squarespace 7.1 version are faster, cleaner, and more versatile than websites built on the old Squarespace 7.0 version.

But if your website has any of the following, it may be worth reconsidering whether migrating from version 7.0 to 7.1 is the best choice for you:

  1. You’ve been grandfathered into a low annual or monthly subscription.
    At the time of writing this, a Business Plan is $23/mo if paid annually, and $33/mo if paid monthly. Some clients I’ve worked with in the past created their Squarespace website many years back, when the subscriptions were as low as $15/mo. If you migrate from 7.0 to 7.1, you’ll be starting a new website, which means you’ll have to say goodbye to your cheaper plan. Make sure you check how much you’re paying now, and compare it to Squarespace’s current pricing before you do the switchover.

  2. You’re happy with your existing site.
    Squarespace version 7.1 offers new features such as the Fluid Engine (a grid-like drag-and-drop content editing experience) and site-wide animations. But if you’re happy with your website now, and don’t need to add any bells and whistles, you’re good to stay on 7.0. As of now, Squarespace still offers support for both versions, so there’s really no added benefit in switching over.

  3. You have lots of complex pages… or a lot of pages in general.
    It’s relatively easy to migrate text to a new 7.1 site — if you like copying and pasting. But if you have lots of complex pages on your website (ex. long pages with multiple images, galleries, videos, etc), it just might not be worth the hassle. If you still insist on switching over and don’t want to do it yourself, you can contact me for an hourly quote to handle the migration.

  4. You have a Member Area with lots of members.
    It’s not an easy process to migrate members from one version to the next. If you’re using Squarespace’s Member Areas, make sure you know what you’re getting yourself into. You can learn more on Squarespace’s support page.

Overall, if you’re looking for speed, a cleaner look, and SEO improvement, then migrating to 7.1 may be the direction you want to go. However, if you’re happy with your 7.0 website and don’t need to add any new features that 7.1 offers, there may not be a compelling reason to upgrade.
summary: Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.

title: How Often Should You Update Your Website?
excerpt: You may see conflicting information about whether or not it’s advantageous to update your website regularly. What’s the real answer?
body:
As you start looking into optimizing your website for SEO purposes, you may see conflicting information about whether or not it’s advantageous to update your website regularly. What’s the real answer?

According to Will Coombe, author of 3 Months to No. 1: The “No-Nonsense” SEO Playbook For Getting Your Website Found on Google, Google rewards freshness. Since relevance is a big Google ranking factor, it stands to reason that new content must equate to relevant (a.k.a. useful) content. Regular website updates show search engines that your website is relevant and current, which may result in higher search engine rankings over time.

For this reason, one of the best things you can do for your website in terms of giving it an SEO boost is exactly what you’re reading now - a blog. A blog is the best way to continually add new content to your website without clogging existing important pages on your website with paragraphs of text.

If you decide to start a blog or already have an existing one, don’t try and outsmart Google by just changing the date the blog posts were released in the hopes of being boosted. Instead, link to older blog posts from your new ones to show that they’re still relevant. Google will recognize when crawling your website.

If you’re looking for a good place to start improving your SEO ranking, begin by posting 1-2 blog posts per week. I know - it sounds like such a hassle. But it’s worth it. One of the highest-ranking websites I’ve worked on in the past was a resource for AP Government high school teachers. This website posted a new “class starter” every day of the week in a blog-like format, which greatly improved its SEO ranking in the long term.

Don’t think you’re a very good writer? Consider hiring a copywriter on Fiverr who specializes in SEO-friendly blog posts, provided the content isn’t too technical. One post will cost you anywhere from $20 - $100. Make sure to read through the reviews and/or ask for a writing sample to make sure that their writing style matches what you’re looking for.

Are you a pretty decent writer but don’t have the time? Consider a copywriting AI tool to help. An AI copywriting tool is essentially computer-generated writing. You can find a list of the best AI copyrighting tools on Neil Patel’s website. From my experience, they aren’t perfect, and won’t generate a perfect blog post from one or two sentences, but they’ll help you fill in the blanks where it’s needed.

Conclusion

In general, it's recommended to update your website with fresh and relevant content at least once a month to maintain a steady flow of new information for your visitors and search engines. This could be in the form of blog posts, new product descriptions, or other types of content that are relevant to your target audience.

When it comes to improving your website for SEO, it’s important to remember: quality over quantity. Instead of simply updating for the sake of updating, you should focus on making intentional updates that bring value to your website viewers.

Remember, SEO ranking improvement is a slow climb - not a sprint.
summary: You may see conflicting information about whether or not it’s advantageous to update your website regularly. What’s the real answer?

title: How Much Should It Cost To Build a Website?
excerpt: The answer to this question depends on many factors such as features, complexity, and designer experience.
body:
How much should it cost to build a website? The answer to this question depends on many factors that I’ll get into in this article. Generally, basic websites can be built for as low as $500 or less, but more complex sites could cost up to $10,000 or more.

How many pages do you want your website to have?

The number of pages and features will determine how much time it takes to build your website. For example, an eCommerce website will take considerably longer than a simple landing page because there's usually much more setup involved. A typical eCommerce website setup involves loading products (pricing, quantity, variants), shipping, taxes, payment processors, etc.

At the time of writing this, the most affordable website package that I offer goes for $1,500, which includes up to three pages, and is perfect for small businesses with a limited budget that just wants a quick, simple website up and running with no bells and whistles required. The most premium website package that I offer starts at $4,400, and it includes up to ten pages. The price may vary depending on whether you need more complex features such as eCommerce, membership, a blog, etc.

How experienced is the designer?

Unsurprisingly, a seasoned web designer will be able to create a website faster than someone new to it. When I first started building Squarespace websites (about 4 years ago), it took me about 3x longer to build a site than it does now, but my prices reflected that.

If you’re on a limited budget and aren’t itching to meet a deadline, you should consider hiring a web designer that’s newer to the industry. Just make sure that you ask for past work to make sure that they’re capable of producing the quality of work that you’re looking for.

How many revisions do you want?

Ask yourself, are you a decisive or indecisive person? After you receive the first draft of your website, you’re going to be expected to send revisions. If you’re a decisive person who generally is good at giving direction, it’s probably going to take you less time (and therefore less money) to push the draft towards completion. If you’d consider yourself a pretty indecisive person who likes to see changes on your website before you decide on them, it might take you several rounds of revisions. If these revisions fall outside the scope of the website package you purchased, it might cost you more money.

If you’d consider yourself an indecisive person - I understand! Your website is a reflection of your business, so you want it to be exactly what you imagined. It’s helpful to provide inspiration sites to give as much guidance as possible if you're going for a specific look and feel. Sometimes it’s hard to convey exactly what you feel like the website is lacking, and inspiration sites do a great job at helping you get the message across to your designer.

Do you want a website built from scratch or on a CMS such as Squarespace, WordPress or Wix?

Building a website from scratch will take a web developer much longer to build than if they were to use a CMS. A CMS (Content Management System) is a pre-built platform that makes it easy for people to create a website without the use of code. The most popular CMS platforms today are Squarespace, WordPress, Shopify, and Wix.

A CMS-built website will suffice for most small businesses. However, if your website needs complex features such as a multi-step checkout process or a very uniquely custom design (think elaborate animations), you'll want to hire a developer who can code it from scratch. Beware - this is the much more costly path to take.

I design all my websites on Squarespace. I personally think it’s the most user-friendly CMS to use, which still allows for simple custom coding tweaks to make the site look original, while still maintaining its editability.
summary: The answer to this question depends on many factors such as features, complexity, and designer experience.
